chapter: Philadelphia and the McRae Brothers Band, 1908-1929
title: McRae Brothers close at Club Ebony; brothers leave for Buffalo
summary: McRae dates the band's New York stay to 1929; after the Club Ebony closed at Thanksgiving, Bill and Floyd went to Buffalo and he stayed in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Before you went to New York, you were with June Clark.
No. This is when we came into New York.
After leaving Atlantic City, we came -- like I told you, we worked at this club and we also broadcast.
But we worked around New York -- I think just before Thanksgiving. This band didn't stay -- we came in around -- we closed after Labor Day in Atlantic City.
You weren't quite 20 at this time. I guess you were out of high school by this time.

Yeah. So, when we came to New York -- We came to New York around '29. It was the year '29. 1929 when we came to New York. Because we played Atlantic City the summer of '29, see. We came into New York and we played -- we did the broadcasts and we played -- did some gigs at the Savoy one night up here. And we worked at this club, 129th Street. That's where we stayed there. And the club closed.

Yeah, Club Ebony. We closed there I think like Thanksgiving Eve, or something. After that, Thanksgiving Day we were off. Because I know we were standing on the corner and one of my brothers said some of the guys wanted to go back to Baltimore, some of them want to
